status: Completed and visually accepted by Tim 2026-11-03, including final water surface/reflection/inland banks and coastal playtest. Representative-load performance and documented edge checks remain.
setup: Three.js 0.186.1 WebGLRenderer, fixed isometric OrthographicCamera, one custom painted ground ShaderMaterial per streamed chunk, shared time/day-night/lantern lighting, existing rounded water mask and coast ribbons.
localFindings: Before the follow-up, island water scrolled a cropped photographic color texture through four repeat phases under a strong static noise warp. Color features blended into one another during animation.
Before the follow-up, the shader had no changing surface normal or broad daylight wave highlights; its extra ripple expression only modulated nighttime lantern light.

Inference from code plus Tim's motion report: moving/morphing the color pattern without independently moving surface-light cues likely causes the thick or magma-like appearance. A still screenshot alone cannot verify the animation.
The seam correction works visually; retain its safe source window and independent-axis continuity. Tim likes the coastline and biome-ground transition, so preserve those.

sources.finding: Official matching-major Three.js implementation uses two animated normal maps, phased flow, Fresnel reflection weighting and reflection/refraction textures. Its full helper also performs extra reflection and refraction scene renders.

Cyan Worlds developer describes layered periodic waves with analytically derived surface normals, separating broad shape from finer texture-space ripples. Fine waves strongly affect perceived water realism. Historical implementation, used here for stable rendering principles rather than modern performance claims.

Author's shader implementation demonstrates seamless flow phases and derivative/normal-map animation; emphasizes the light response of the surface rather than relying on animated albedo alone. Unity syntax requires adaptation to our GLSL.

recommendation: Keep the current chunk renderer and seam-safe base, with restrained color-pattern movement and much weaker large-scale warping. Keep contrast controlled so painted white features do not dominate as melting shapes.

Add two or three coherent directional wave components plus finer ripples, animated in world space. Initially compute slopes/normals analytically in the fragment shader; a dedicated seamless normal/derivative texture is an optional later refinement, not an initial art requirement.

Drive moving soft highlights and a restrained sky-colored surface sheen from the changing normals. Use the fixed orthographic VIEW_DIR, existing painterly palette, day/night grade and lantern lights. Do not use a per-fragment perspective view vector that makes an orthographic surface shade incorrectly.
Retain original water mask, rounded shoreline, ground transition and collisions. Clip all surface effects to water. Share wave phase by world position and common time so streaming chunk edges agree.

If the first surface pass needs it, add restrained water-side shoreline foam later from the same rounded shore distance. Do not generate a tiled white foam grid, paint foam onto land, or change the accepted beach art.

Start with open-ocean motion. Expose cosmetic calmness/flow settings for later lake, river and marsh water profiles using actual water classification; this does not authorize reshaping rivers, lakes, sources or crossings.

tradeoffs.fullWater2Helper: Compatible with WebGLRenderer, but reflection/refraction scene passes and a separate water mesh per ground chunk would be an architectural/performance change. Adapt its wave/lighting principles into our shader first; do not instantiate a helper per chunk.
tradeoffs.analyticNormals: No new image assets or reflection render targets initially. Extra fragment math requires measurement; avoid evaluating expensive water shading over inland pixels where possible.
tradeoffs.limitations: Stylized surface lighting on a flat water plane does not provide a displaced ocean silhouette, real scene reflections, wave physics or boat buoyancy. Those are not required for this proposed camera/style pass.

boundaries: Completed accepted water/reflection/inland-bank pass; no fluid simulation or boat physics. Representative-load performance unmeasured.

implementation.changes: Four authored wave components (two broad/two fine) drive analytical slopes, orthographic-view sheen and soft moving highlights. Base texture drift is much weaker with tiny ripple distortion; strong noise warping is removed from the enabled path. Existing safe source window and independent-axis phase blending retained. Explicit texture gradients avoid false mip blur at tile wraps and water-mask branches. Pixel-footprint filtering damps subpixel waves. Expensive water shading is skipped on fully inland pixels.
implementation.scope: Final pass includes shared reflection capture, procedural normal fields and inland-bank integration; earlier first-pass scope superseded.
implementation.validation: Edited modules pass node --check; configured packets are finite, preserve authored world wavelengths/speeds and have a maximum slope bound of 0.249. test_p3_edges still passes (90,000 collision samples, rounded geometry, masks/halos, exclusions and bounded movement). Scoped diff whitespace check passed. No live WebGL compile, visual result or measured GPU cost claimed.
implementation.remaining: Visual review passed; retain representative-load performance and documented corner/crossing checks.

secondPassProposal.feedback: Repeated white motifs in the source color tile still dominate the open water. The first pass added analytical ripple lighting, not the complete Three.js water material.
secondPassProposal.recommended: Subdued lighter blue-green base, shared normal/derivative-map wave detail and soft view-angle reflection. Keep the successful shoreline masks and anti-banding. Reduce the repeated painted foam motifs instead of merely brightening them.
secondPassProposal.reflection: Start with one shared low-resolution reflection capture for all visible coplanar water, sampled only through the existing water mask. Optional sky-only mode provides a cheaper fallback. Do not create a reflection/refraction helper for every streamed chunk.

proposedBudget.estimateLimits: Allocation arithmetic only, not measured total RAM/VRAM. Excludes CPU decoded images, driver allocations and any other render buffers. Exact depth format and mip handling vary.

secondPassProposal.mainCost: A real reflection adds a scene render; GPU/frame time and sprite rendering cost need manual measurement. Memory is bounded with one shared target. Stock Water2 creates both reflection and refraction helpers, whose current defaults include four-sample MSAA; avoid those defaults for a memory-conscious prototype.
secondPassProposal.camera: Reflector in r186 handles cloned cameras, but our fixed isometric billboard art still needs visual validation in reflected views. Use orthographic-compatible capture and existing day/night grading.
secondPassProposal.approval: Approved, implemented and visually accepted; original proposal retained for rationale.
